title: Regional policy-driven evidence collector for automated SOC2/ISO attestations
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a region-aware evidence collection service and orchestration layer that automatically gathers, normalizes, and stores control artifacts for SOC 2 and ISO 27001 attestations. The collector must enforce per-region residency and retention policies, tag evidence with immutable provenance metadata, and emit auditable events to the evidence ledger. Targets: support hosted and private deployments, map artifacts to SOC2 trust criteria and ISO Annex A controls, and enable scheduled attestations and one-click exports for auditors.
acceptance_criteria: Collector can be configured with region-specific residency and retention rules (e.g., EU, US, APAC) and enforces them by routing storage to applicable buckets or on-prem vaults.
Every collected artifact includes immutable metadata: collector_id, region_tag, policy_version, timestamp, source_request_id, and hash.

Control-to-artifact mapping table auto-populates for SOC2 and ISO27001 (e.g., CC6.1, CC3.2, A.9.2) with at least 12 mapped artifact types (audit logs, access attestations, backup snapshots, config drift reports).
Evidence ledger exposes an append-only timeline and API for auditors to query artifacts by control, region, and retention window.
Retention enforcement schedule runs nightly and produces a retention-audit report showing deletions and archival moves with signed acknowledgements.
Playbook and UI in Console for creating a scheduled attestation bundle and exporting a time-bounded evidence package (.tar.gz + checksum).
Integration tests with Dedicated and Private deployments validate routing to customer-managed buckets and KMS-wrapped keys.
notes: Implementation will combine a lightweight collector daemon (running in host or sidecar) + central orchestration service that stores metadata in the evidence ledger (append-only event store).

Trade-off: centralizing metadata improves search but increases attack surface. Mitigation: metadata is minimal and encrypted in transit and at-rest; sensitive blobs stored in customer-owned storage when requested.
We will use policy-as-code (Rego or similar) to express residency+retention rules so non-engineers can modify policies via Console with audit trail.
Will reuse existing logging and snapshot exporters from ENG-3345 to avoid duplicating telemetry exporters; collector focuses on enrichment and tagging.
Retention model: hot (<90 days) in fast storage, cold (90-365) archived with index, expired (>policy) either deleted or moved to long-term vault per customer setting.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Asha Patel: Created ticket. Scope focused on residency+retention tagging, ledger, and attestation export. Asked ENG to validate feasibility for Private deployments.
2026-03-03 - Michael Chen: Spiked a collector sidecar prototype. Confirmed ability to attach KMS-wrapped pointers for customer-owned storage. See spike notes link.
2026-03-05 - Sofia Alvarez (Design): Reviewed UI flows for scheduling attestations. Suggested adding a dry-run retention audit mode so customers can preview deletions.
2026-03-08 - Security review request submitted to SecOps. Raised question about metadata sensitivity — decision: store hashes and pointers, not raw secrets.
2026-03-10 - Michael Chen: Implemented initial metadata schema and event contract; pushing WIP branch for early review (PR #148).
decision_log: Decided to implement policy-as-code to keep residency/retention rules declarative and versioned.
Decision to emit minimal metadata centrally and keep raw artifacts in customer-controlled storage when possible to reduce risk.
Chosen to prioritize export format as signed tarball + manifest (JSON) for auditor consumption, rather than custom viewer.
